overall_summary: Analysis of 47 deduplicated Shorts reveals a stark performance divide: first-person hypothetical space survival hooks ('What If You Fell Into...') and extreme cosmic body anomalies drive channel peaks (800–1,050+ views, up to 38 likes), while generic psychology and repeated low-effort trivia (fake memories, earworms, silent space) fail under 100 views. Videos between 19–21 seconds significantly outperform 12–16 second clips. Furthermore, exact duplicate re-uploads consistently decay in reach across consecutive attempts.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person Hypothetical Threat Hook ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) led engagement and reach.
winning_patterns.action: Frame high-concept cosmic and extreme science phenomena as direct second-person survival scenarios ('What If You...').

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice...' (1,057 views), 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,031 views, 36 likes), and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views) dominate top percentiles.
winning_patterns.action: Focus subject selection on extreme astrophysical anomalies with shocking sensory contrasts (fire, darkness, crushing pressure).

winning_patterns.evidence: Top 5 performers all have runtimes between 19 and 21 seconds, allowing enough narrative buildup for a satisfying payoff without pacing drag.
winning_patterns.action: Target scripts specifically for 19–21 seconds (approximately 45–55 spoken words) with brisk visual cuts.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5–53 views across 3 uploads) and earworm trivia (17–71 views) generated virtually zero viewer traction or engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Cease repetitive cognitive/psychology trivia unless packaged with visceral stakes or historical mystery.

weak_patterns.evidence: Duplicate concepts ('Why Space Is Completely Silent' posted 3 times: 220 -> 87 -> 34 views; octopus heart facts posted 3 times) experienced sharp algorithmic decay.
weak_patterns.action: Enforce strict uniqueness across content pipelines; never re-upload identical hooks or facts without substantial narrative re-engineering.

next_video.opening_direction: Instantly immerse the viewer in the cockpit of a ship falling toward a spinning neutron star with magnetic lines warping spacetime.

next_video.reason: Directly leverages the highest-performing hook framework ('What If You...') applied to an extreme astrophysical terror (Magnetar SGR 1806-20) not yet featured on the channel.
